editorial:
Imagine moving to a big city where you don't know anyone and everyone seems to judge you. That is exactly what Gyeong-hwan goes through in this sweet, nostalgic story. He is a shy kid just trying to survive high school in Daegu back in 2001. Things change when he meets Jae-min, the popular class president who is actually a great guy. They bond over old Japanese pop music and a shared sense of loneliness. The vibe is very soft and cozy, making you feel like you are stepping back into the early 2000s with your own old friends.

The acting is what really makes this work because the chemistry between the two leads feels totally real. You will love how the movie focuses on the small, quiet moments of their friendship. While the pace is a bit slow at times, it helps you feel the weight of their emotions. If you enjoy stories about first loves and finding where you belong, you need to see this.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a jump to the present day, showing that Gyeong-hwan and Jae-min drifted apart after high school due to societal pressure. However, they reunite as adults at a music cafe. They realize that their feelings for each other never truly went away. Instead of hiding who they are like they did in 2001, they decide to finally be together, proving that some bonds are too strong to break over time.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about first love and nostalgic settings.
